findings.message: `scan` now drops any stem with no committed blob on main. A new ticket that intake refuses (for example invalid frontmatter) stays on disk uncommitted, so `git show` raises `GitError` and the stem is skipped. It never appears in `current`, `watch` never yields it, and the Watcher never parses it, so `watcher_parse_failure` is never journaled. `scan` also discards intake's `refused` result, so `serve` now reports the bad ticket nowhere. Before this diff the stem was yielded and the signal was journaled. `test_serve_watcher_edits_deletions_and_last_good` only covers an already-committed stem, so it misses this. The ticket did not ask for this filter, and the boundary check already holds a run whose ticket is dirty.
findings.paved_road: Restore `{stem: self.read(stem) for stem in self.stems()}` in `scan`. If a filter is still needed, it must keep yielding stems with no committed blob so the Watcher reports them, and a serve test must cover an invalid new stem producing `watcher_parse_failure`.

findings.message: `_admit` runs `ticket_changed` before it reads the retained hold's state, so two paths that are not merge admissions get the hold. (1) Kill: when a held stem has a `reject` release and its ticket was edited, the result is `gate_failed`/`ticket_changed` in the Reject queue. The `rejected` transition, `_dead_dependents` and `retire` are all skipped, so the operator's kill is lost and has to be repeated. (2) Landed squash: when `merge/<stem>/<attempt>` has already completed but a crash came before the `merged` terminal, the latest transition is still `running`. An edit then journals `gate_failed` and removes the worktree for work already on main, and a keep re-runs it. The check added to `reconstruct` at line 219 has the same ordering problem for both cases.
findings.paved_road: Check `ticket_changed` only on the path that would still admit. For a retained stem, run it after the `reject` release branch and the `completed` squash branch, and before the `_finish` and rebase paths. In `reconstruct`, skip the check when the hold has a reject release or a completed squash effect, and let `_admit` settle those. Add tests for a kill and for a completed squash on a held stem with an edited ticket.
